technical_and_design_decisions: Implement acceptance tests as black-box integration tests using the repository's existing acceptance-test framework and conventions.
Reuse existing test fixtures, assertions, build plugins, and CI profiles wherever available rather than introducing a new testing framework.
Cover the normal successful processing path and the principal module-specific validation behavior for each processor or sink.
Use isolated test data and temporary resources so tests are repeatable and safe to run on every CI build.
Use containerized or embedded test doubles for external HDFS and mail dependencies when the existing project infrastructure supports them.
Keep production module code unchanged unless testability defects are discovered; any minor test-support changes will be included in the relevant activity.
Integrate all tests into the standard CI lifecycle and ensure they are enabled by default.
assumptions: The eight processor and sink modules already exist and their intended behavior is documented sufficiently in source code, configuration metadata, or existing unit tests.
An acceptance-test harness and standard project build are already available; effort includes extending them but not creating a complete testing platform from scratch.
The developer has access to the repository, can run the build locally, and can modify test and CI configuration.
No new product functionality is required beyond acceptance-test coverage.
The json-tuple, splitter, gauge, aggregate-counter, and field-value-counter tests can run without provisioning complex external infrastructure.
The script and scripts modules require coverage of their supported scripting configuration and representative execution behavior, but not exhaustive coverage of every supported scripting language.
HDFS and mail acceptance tests may use local, embedded, mocked, or containerized dependencies consistent with the existing project setup.
CI execution time and infrastructure capacity are sufficient for the added tests; performance optimization beyond avoiding obvious flakiness is out of scope.
Estimates include implementation, local execution, defect correction, and review-ready test documentation, but exclude waiting time for external approvals or CI infrastructure provisioning.

activities.activity_description: Inspect module implementations, existing unit and acceptance tests, build profiles, CI configuration, test conventions, and available external-service fixtures; map each user story to concrete acceptance scenarios.
Add or adapt shared fixtures, input data, assertions, lifecycle setup, cleanup, and configuration needed to support the new module-level acceptance tests.
Implement acceptance scenarios for json-tuple input transformation, expected tuple or JSON output, configuration, and failure or edge behavior appropriate to the existing project conventions.

activities.activity_name: script and scripts processor acceptance coverage
activities.activity_description: Implement acceptance coverage for both script processor modules, including representative script execution, configuration differences, produced output, and relevant error handling.
Implement acceptance scenarios validating splitting behavior, emitted records, ordering or grouping expectations, configuration, and handling of representative input data.
Implement acceptance coverage proving that gauge records are accepted and written or exposed through the expected sink behavior, using the project's available verification mechanism.
Implement acceptance scenarios validating aggregation, counter updates, output or persistence, and representative reset or grouping behavior supported by the module.
Implement acceptance scenarios validating counting by configured field values, expected results, and handling of representative records and missing or alternative field values.
Implement acceptance coverage for dataset creation or writing to HDFS, including path or partition configuration, persisted content verification, cleanup, and external-service fixture handling.

Implement acceptance coverage for message construction and delivery through the mail sink, using a local test mail server or equivalent fixture and verifying relevant headers, recipient, subject, and body behavior.
Register all tests in the appropriate build modules and profiles, configure required dependencies or test services, and ensure the tests execute as part of every standard CI build.
Run the complete suite repeatedly, diagnose and correct failures or flakiness, verify isolation and cleanup, review test naming and diagnostics, and document any required test-service or CI settings.
